title: Styling in React Native
description: Learn how to apply styles and design UI components in React Native.

quiz.question: How do you create styles in React Native?
quiz.explanation: React Native uses StyleSheet.create to define styles in JavaScript.

quiz.question: Which property is used to set background color in React Native styles?
quiz.explanation: The 'backgroundColor' property sets the background color of a component.

quiz.question: How do you apply multiple styles to a React Native component?
options: Using a string of class names
quiz.explanation: Multiple styles can be applied by passing an array to the 'style' prop.

quiz.question: What unit is used for measurements like width and height in React Native?
quiz.explanation: React Native uses density-independent pixels to ensure consistent sizing across devices.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid flexbox property in React Native?
quiz.explanation: 'float' is not supported in React Native; flexbox is used for layout.

quiz.question: How do you make a component fill all available space in its container?
quiz.explanation: Setting flex: 1 makes the component expand to fill available space.

quiz.question: Which property controls the font size of text in React Native?
quiz.explanation: 'fontSize' controls the size of the text.

quiz.question: Can you use CSS classes in React Native styling?
quiz.explanation: React Native does not support CSS classes; styling is done via JavaScript objects.

quiz.question: How do you create a style for a React Native component that changes based on props?
options: By conditionally applying styles in the component
quiz.correctAnswer: By conditionally applying styles in the component
quiz.explanation: You can apply styles conditionally in the render method based on props.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of StyleSheet.flatten()?
options: To combine multiple style objects into one
quiz.correctAnswer: To combine multiple style objects into one
quiz.explanation: StyleSheet.flatten merges an array of styles into a single object.
